final_recommendation: The room converged on a trilateral package framework: 75% auto RVC with 18-month phase-in (Jan 2020), six-year sunset with auto-renewal unless formal objection 18 months prior, labor enforcement through trilateral panel with binding 30-day findings and automatic tariffs after 60-day remedy window, and Canada's phased dairy concessions (18/24 months with quarterly reviews). Critical implementation details remain contested—dairy tariff percentages, sunset objection threshold mechanics, and labor panel investigative authority—but the core structure is ratifiable.
minority_objections: dairy_ag demanded locked tariff percentages (15%+10% cheese, 18%+12% powder) versus USTR's day-one cuts (20% cheese, 25% powder)
supply_chain_mfr raised unresolved concern about sunset objection threshold—whether one country's letter triggers renegotiation or requires higher bar
key_conflicts: Chapter 19 dispute settlement: Canada insisted it stays for goods disputes, USTR initially demanded removal, ultimately Canada preserved it while accepting separate labor panel
Dairy tariff cuts: USTR demanded 20%/25% day-one cuts, Canada countered with 18/24-month phase-in with quarterly reviews, percentages remained contested

Labor enforcement sovereignty: Mexico insisted violations go to Mexican courts, labor_union demanded automatic tariffs, compromise landed on trilateral panel with 30-day findings and 60-day remedy window before automatic tariffs
key_concessions: Canada accepted phased dairy opening (18 months cheese, 24 months powder with quarterly reviews) after initially calling 20%/25% cuts 'dismantling supply management'
USTR accepted Chapter 19 preservation for goods disputes after initially declaring it 'off the table'
Mexico accepted trilateral labor panel with binding findings and automatic tariff trigger, moving from initial position of domestic-only enforcement
Hard sunset clause converted to six-year review with auto-renewal mechanism, addressing business uncertainty concerns
red_lines: Canada: Chapter 19 dispute settlement for goods must remain ('Parliament won't ratify without it')
Canada: Supply management core structure preserved, only marginal opening acceptable
Mexico: Labor enforcement cannot involve 'U.S. inspectors on Mexican soil'
USTR/Congress: Labor enforcement must have 'real teeth'—binding findings and tariff consequences, not 'slow arbitration track'
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Sunset objection threshold mechanics left undefined despite supply_chain_mfr warning about investment uncertainty ('won't commit tooling spend in 2020 if agreement gets shaken up in 2026')
Specific dairy tariff percentages remained contested at close—dairy_ag's locked phase-in percentages versus USTR's day-one cuts never fully reconciled
Labor panel investigative authority and violation trigger definition left vague despite us_congress demanding clarity on 'who investigates violations, what triggers the 60-day clock'
Supply chain compliance costs and sourcing adjustment timelines raised but not systematically addressed in final package structure
downstream_risk_variables: Congressional ratification depends on final labor panel text specifying investigative authority and tariff trigger clarity
Canadian parliamentary ratification hinges on dairy phase-in percentages and quarterly review implementation
Business investment decisions frozen until sunset objection threshold defined
Auto supplier reorganization costs and potential plant closures if 75% RVC phase-in compressed
Mexico's domestic labor court capacity to meet 30-day finding deadlines
Dairy_ag constituency support conditional on locked tariff cut percentages not yet finalized
uncertainty_notes: Package structure agreed but critical implementation details unresolved: (1) dairy tariff cut percentages—USTR's 20%/25% versus dairy_ag's phased 15%+10%/18%+12% never reconciled; (2) sunset auto-renewal objection threshold—whether single-country letter or higher bar triggers renegotiation undefined; (3) labor panel investigative authority and violation trigger mechanics—who investigates, what evidence standard, what starts 60-day clock left vague; (4) auto RVC phase-in supplier-level timelines and compliance cost allocation not specified.

marker_evidence.auto_rules_bottleneck: 75% RVC with 18-month phase-in became the concrete timeline that unlocked package progress—auto_industry and us_congress explicitly tied ratification to this timeline, and it drove final convergence ('Congress can defend that to their districts')
marker_evidence.labor_enforcement_key: Labor enforcement structure—trilateral panel with binding 30-day findings and automatic tariffs after 60-day remedy window—was the 'strongest labor provision yet proposed' and 'directly addresses Congress's ratification concerns'; us_congress stated 'Congress votes no' without this clarity
marker_evidence.canada_dairy_final_issue: Dairy concessions were Canada's core political concession ('dismantling supply management') and dairy_ag made ratification conditional on specific cuts ('we don't have a deal my constituency will support'); phased opening (18/24 months) was the compromise that moved Canada from 'walk' threat to package acceptance
marker_evidence.dispute_settlement_canada_redline: Canada stated 'Chapter 19 stays—that's not negotiable, and you know Parliament won't ratify without it'; USTR initially demanded removal, ultimately accepted it for goods disputes while separating labor enforcement—this was the structural compromise that enabled trilateral package
marker_evidence.sunset_to_review_compromise: Hard sunset clause converted to six-year review with auto-renewal unless formal objection 18 months prior—us_congress secured 'explicit confirmation' of this language, and it directly reduced sunset_uncertainty and us_ratification_risk in GM scoring; this compromise resolved business uncertainty concerns
marker_evidence.ratification_risk: us_congress explicitly conditioned ratification on labor panel clarity ('Congress votes no regardless of your RVC timeline' without enforcement details), dairy_ag made constituency support conditional on tariff cuts, and auto_industry tied phase-in timeline to avoiding 'plant closures tied to new NAFTA'—ratification constraints shaped every major concession
marker_evidence.supply_chain_adjustment: supply_chain_mfr raised compliance costs ('retooling costs and sourcing shifts'), phase-in needs ('12-18 month phase-in so suppliers can actually reorganize'), and sunset investment uncertainty ('won't commit tooling spend'), but these concerns were acknowledged and then addressed through phase-in timeline rather than driving separate structural changes
marker_evidence.us_mexico_first_pressures_canada: Mexico set hard deadline ('bilateral holds through Friday—that's real') and USTR explicitly leveraged it ('there's no trilateral package and Mexico and I move forward without you')—this time pressure drove Canada's dairy concessions and Chapter 19 compromise; mexico_neg stated 'I'm not walking away from a done package' once Canada moved
